puzzles.title: Count the vowels
puzzles.hook: How many vowels are in a sentence?
puzzles.md: Return how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u, upper or lower case) are in `text`.
puzzles.start:
def count_vowels(text):          #> take some text
    count = 0                      #> no vowels yet
    for ch in text:                #> look at each letter
        if ch == "a":             #> TODO: only checks for a lowercase a
            count += 1             #> one more vowel
    return count                   #> how many
puzzles.fast:
def count_vowels(text):          #> take some text
    count = 0                      #> no vowels yet
    for ch in text.lower():        #> look at each letter, in lower case
        if ch in "aeiou":         #> is it a vowel?
            count += 1             #> one more vowel
    return count                   #> how many
hints: Upper and lower case both count: try lowering the text first.
`ch in "aeiou"` checks all five vowels at once.

scale.text: Search engines count and index letters and words across billions of pages with exactly this kind of single pass.

puzzles.title: Missing number
puzzles.hook: One number from 0 to n is missing. Which one?
puzzles.md: `nums` holds every number from 0 to n except one. Return the missing number.
puzzles.start:
def missing(nums):               #> take the numbers
    for x in range(len(nums) + 1): #> try every number from 0 to n
        if x not in nums:          #> is it absent? (this scans the whole list!)
            return x               #> found the missing one
puzzles.fast:
def missing(nums):               #> take the numbers
    n = len(nums)                  #> n numbers are here, so they go up to n
    expected = n * (n + 1) // 2    #> what 0 + 1 + … + n adds up to
    return expected - sum(nums)    #> the gap is the missing number
hints: `x not in nums` looks through the whole list every time.
You know what 0 + 1 + … + n adds up to. What does that tell you?

scale.text: Checksums work the same way: add everything up, and a missing piece shows up as a gap in the total.

ideas.title: How your card number catches typos by itself
ideas.hook: One digit at the end checks all the others.
ideas.brief: The Luhn algorithm (Hans Peter Luhn, IBM, 1954) adds a check digit to card numbers: double every second digit from the right, subtract 9 from results over 9, add everything up; a valid number's total ends in 0. It catches every single-digit typo and most swaps of neighbouring digits, so shops reject mistyped numbers before contacting the bank.
